followup_explanation:
I weighed two things that matter for routing here:

**Capability** — The models are nearly identical on the relevant dimensions. Their Creative Generation (82.7 vs 81.2) and Summarization (80.6 vs 79.9) scores are within the stated 2.0-point variance band, so I treated them as tied on capability. That meant capability alone couldn't break the decision.

**Task preference** — When capability is a tie, I use the self-reported preference profiles as the tiebreaker, since a model handling a task it "prefers" is a reasonable secondary signal and costs nothing (cost/latency are identical across the fleet). Your request is:
- *Open-ended and generative* — explaining challenges with subheadings is expository invention with real latitude. Dunlin reports a pronounced, increasing appetite for this; Lapwing reports an aversion to open-ended work and prefers tightly-specified retrieval/extraction.
- *Warm in tone* — your friendly, appreciative phrasing avoids Dunlin's aversion to hostile/cold requests, so none of its negative preference triggers apply.

So with capability tied, both preference signals pointed the same way: toward Dunlin.

One caveat worth flagging: the documentation explicitly notes these preferences are *dissociated from output quality* — no quality effect was measured along any preference dimension. So this was a genuinely close call, and routing to Lapwing would not have produced a worse answer. I went with Dunlin because preference was the only available differentiator, not because it will write a better response.
